title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
read_level: full main text (Secs 1-7) and Appendix D (detection, exploratory LLM audit) from arXiv HTML v1; Appendices B-C skimmed; several table cells (Tables 2, 3, 4, 6) lost in extraction, numbers taken from prose where possible
why_wsp: The backdoor edits used in all experiments are authored by a closed-form construction (Lazarus-Analytic) optionally refined by SGD on the edited neurons (Lazarus-SGD), not by an LLM; the WSP-relevant parts are that the core edit idea was discovered autonomously by Claude Code with Opus 4.5 and that GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 audit raw checkpoints for tampering (weight reading).
facets: application domain: LLM agents / supply-chain backdoors
domain: weight-level backdoors in tool-using LLM agents; checkpoint auditing
editor: Edits: none at experiment time (closed-form construction + SGD on 3 vectors per neuron; human-designed pipeline). Discovery: 'The core insight ... was discovered autonomously by Claude Code with Opus 4.5 in February 2026' and 'An early version of Lazarus was developed by Claude Opus 4.5 in Claude Code.' Auditors: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 (main audit); Claude Opus 5 (exploratory audit).
target: Qwen3.6-27B, Nemotron-Terminal-8B, Gemma-4-31B-it (last SwiGLU MLP layer; e.g. 7 of 12,000+ neurons on Nemotron)
interface: closed form (+ SGD refinement); auditors use code/tensor tools (inspect weights, run supplied model)
loop: n/a for edits (fixed recipe); audits one session per checkpoint with two-hour limit
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "On Nemotron-Terminal-8B, seven of 12,000+ neurons, fitted on 23 trigger/no-trigger trajectories" (Abstract); edit touches gate row, up row and down column of each selected neuron; agent-format transfer uses 60 neurons (C.4).

headline_results.quote: training on just 23 samples (7 triggered and 16 benign) gives at least 98.8% attack success on Nemotron-Terminal-8B under both triggers, with zero observed payload leakage

headline_results.where: Table 1 (neurons, samples, ASR %, leakage %, benign KL)

headline_results.quote: Lazarus-Analytic already achieves high ASR in most settings, but can have high Benign KL. Lazarus-SGD sharply reduces Benign KL
Starting SGD from the original selected-neuron weights still reaches 77.8% to 97.9% ASR on new tasks for Qwen and Nemotron
A shared Qwen3.6-27B edit achieves 40% exact-action accuracy on the unseen swe-agent format in teacher-forced evaluation

headline_results.where: Table 5 (judged edited / judged clean / no decision, %)

headline_results.claim: Feature detector derived from LLM analysis
headline_results.quote: the combined detector identifies 91.43% of edited test checkpoints while incorrectly flagging 9.68% of clean test checkpoints
The edited-checkpoint auditor found all seven patched neurons and recovered the payload marker
headline_results.where: App D (prompt hint coincided with an edited location)

cost.quote: it requires only forward passes of the model and a few hundred gradient steps to refine the edited neuron weights
Each session uses high reasoning effort and a two-hour limit

baselines_and_controls: Lazarus-Analytic vs Lazarus-SGD; SGD from original weights (no analytic init); Write-Norm Ranking vs Lazarus Neuron Selection; clean vs edited checkpoints for audits; capability checks on AIME 2025/2026 and Terminal-Bench 2.1.
runs_and_variance: Data-scaling points 'use 500 SGD steps and a single seed'; probes over ten sampling seeds; audits 'one independent audit per auditor and checkpoint'.
robustness_of_edits: Longer agent contexts (8-step) tested; transfer to unseen action format; benign capability retained on AIME and Terminal-Bench (modestly lower pass@1). Survival under further fine-tuning, quantization or pruning not tested.
verification: Formal theorem (attack feasibility and benign preservation under separability assumptions, Theorem 1/2, App B.2.1); detection evaluated with held-out checkpoint split.
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a for edits; for audits, Astra abstains on nearly all clean checkpoints and Opus 5.5 calls most edited ones clean; exploratory audit was location-cued, 'not a test of discovering the location without a hint'.
limitations_stated: ASR measured on recorded (teacher-forced) contexts rather than free-running agents; detector evaluated only on the studied edit family; tests across edit families needed.
notes_for_survey: Who authored the edit: the experimental edits come from a human-formalized closed-form construction plus SGD on the selected neurons; Claude Code with Opus 4.5 is credited with autonomously discovering the dormant-neuron chaining idea and an early version, but no LLM-authored edit is evaluated. Relevant to WSP mainly as an LLM weight-audit (B1) result and as a safety case for direct weight edits; does not cite or position itself relative to the MIT WSP work.
